summary.text: Pat Ryan is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for New York's 18th Congressional District. A West Point graduate and Army intelligence officer who served two combat tours in Iraq, he worked in the technology sector and was Ulster County Executive from 2019 to 2022. He won a 2022 special election in the old NY-19 and was elected to the redrawn NY-18 that November; he sits on the Armed Services and Transportation and Infrastructure committees.

paragraphs.text: Pat Ryan was born and raised in Kingston, New York, and graduated from Kingston High School in 2000; his official biography calls him a fifth-generation Hudson Valley native.

He earned a bachelor's degree in international politics from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point in 2004 and a master's degree in security studies from Georgetown University (2013, per Ballotpedia).
Ryan served in the U.S. Army from 2004 to 2009 as a military intelligence officer; his official biography says he served two combat tours in Iraq and earned two Bronze Stars.

After leaving the Army, Ryan worked as deputy director of Berico Technologies, co-founded the software company Praescient Analytics in 2011, and was a senior vice president at Dataminr from 2015 to 2017, according to Wikipedia.
He ran in the 2018 Democratic primary in NY-19, receiving 18% to Antonio Delgado's 22%.
In April 2019 he won a special election for Ulster County Executive, took office June 7, 2019, and won a full term that November; he resigned on September 9, 2022.
His official biography says he led the county through the COVID-19 pandemic and the redevelopment of the former IBM site, now iPark 87.

Ryan won the August 23, 2022 special election in NY-19 over Dutchess County Executive Marc Molinaro, 51.1% to 48.8%, and was sworn in September 13, 2022; in November 2022 he won the redrawn NY-18, defeating Republican Colin Schmitt.

In the House he serves on the Armed Services Committee and the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, and his official biography describes him as the first West Point graduate to represent the Academy in the U.S. House.
He lives in Gardiner with his wife, Rebecca, and their two sons, according to his official biography.
